title: Market Narratives and the Unpredictable Alpha - Systematic Investor 322

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Market Narratives and the Unpredictable Alpha - Systematic Investor 322.docx

summary:
Systematic Investor 322 (Nov 2024, post-US election): Mark discusses equity risk premium, bond term premium, risk cycle/leverage, why trend followers use prices not narratives, and research on analysts, narratives and trend-following allocation.
Trend following is observational not causal; position sizing matters more than forecasting; economic trends beget price trends.
Views: bond yields can keep rising, equity ERP falling means lower forward stock returns, credit spreads too tight.

ERP measures, analysts backward looking, CTA index performance Nov 2024

completeness_estimate: 0.75 - first reader caught all main themes (ERP, term premium, risk cycle, sizing, analysts, narratives, Quantica) but missed several secondary mechanisms and caveats (rate vol vs level, term premium vs stock-bond correlation, SVB duration risk, EPU noise, event jumps vs underreaction).

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the equity risk premium has now turn negative so if you think that the stock market is going to continue to go higher over the next couple of years
claims.claim: S&P earnings yield minus 10-year Treasury yield has turned negative, signalling weaker long-term equity returns despite post-election euphoria.
claims.conditions: one chart only; use an ensemble of valuation measures
claims.testable: yes - simple series, test forward 1-5y returns

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: then you look at what is the uh forward behavior of stocks over one two five years it's usually lower
claims.claim: A declining equity risk premium is followed on average by lower stock returns over 1, 2 and 5 years, a probabilistic not certain relation.
claims.testable: yes - regress forward returns on ERP

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: it doesn't account for earnings growth so it's just taking the current uh earnings uh dividing it
claims.claim: The simple inverse-P/E equity risk premium ignores earnings growth, so growth-adjusted ERP measures differ in level though similar in direction.
claims.indicator: earnings yield based ERP vs growth-adjusted ERP

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: the gap between kind of what it was was pointing to and people's expectations
claims.claim: Expectations of equity returns are high while forward returns implied by valuation look poor, a gap last seen around 2000.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there's still a preponderance of evidence to show that analysts you know look back in time as opposed to try to forecast in the future
claims.claim: Despite MBA training in discounting forward earnings, evidence shows analysts anchor on past earnings.

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: the sck Gen CTA index up 1.6% month to date bringing the year to date figure to plus 0.9%
claims.claim: SG CTA index up 1.6% mid-November 2024 (YTD +0.9%), trend index +2.7% (YTD +0.55%): equity and bond trends and a dollar spike helped trend followers.
claims.indicator: SG CTA Index, SG Trend Index
claims.direction: long equities, short bonds, long dollar helped

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: people were were starting to be uh less uncertain about the outcome before the actual election occurred
claims.claim: VIX fell about 20 to 15 and began falling before the election as uncertainty resolved; SPX vol term structure moved from backwardation back to contango.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if there is a uh looser tax policy or expectation of lower taxes or lower regulation that's usually better for small cap stocks versus large cap stocks
claims.claim: Lower taxes or lighter regulation favour small caps over large caps because fixed regulatory costs weigh more on small firms; Russell 2000 outperformed after the election.
claims.direction: long small caps vs large caps
claims.conditions: when deregulation or tax cuts are expected
claims.testable: yes - event study of policy regimes

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the long end of the bond market is saying is is that well we're not buying what you're selling
claims.claim: Fed cut 25bp but long yields kept rising, breaking the classic easing-lowers-yields relation; long end trend continued.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: they were going to have the average inflation rate policy
claims.claim: The Fed's average inflation targeting framework has effectively been abandoned.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if there is a lot of policy uncertainty and even from the comments from Paul thought what what will happen then what you see is is that there should be a greater uh risk premium or term premium in bonds
claims.claim: High policy uncertainty (Bloom news and policy uncertainty indices) raises term premia in long bonds and can create divergence between what the Fed wants and market pricing.

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: if um if inflation break evens Rise sufficiently um you know that that that that very much influences uh the Fed
claims.claim: Rising TIPS breakevens can influence the Fed, so the bond market constrains the Fed as well as fiscal policy.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: when the surprise index moves higher that that tells you
claims.claim: Rising economic surprise indices and loose financial conditions are good trend signals supporting higher yields.
claims.indicator: Citi/Bloomberg economic surprise index; financial conditions index; inflation surprise index

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: economic Trends begets price trends if you see the trends in economics are all moving higher then that's going to actually then translate into the price
claims.claim: As a macro trend follower, trends in economic data translate into price trends, so fundamental trends reinforce price trends.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you're more wary if the fundamental data is at odds with what the trend we're seeing
claims.claim: Trend confidence falls if fundamentals disagree: slowing growth, tightening financial conditions or negative surprise index while yields trend up.
claims.indicator: growth nowcast, financial conditions, surprise index
claims.direction: reduce trend exposure when fundamentals conflict

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: look at the Atlantic fed nowcast their GDP let showing up close to 3%
claims.claim: GDPNow near 3% and rising surprise indices reinforce the bond yield uptrend, so it could last longer.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: rates would go higher but the dollar would go lower so that people didn't want to buy the safe assets
claims.claim: In a fiscal-crisis bond vigilante scenario yields would rise with a falling dollar; a rising dollar with rising yields says growth is driving it instead.
claims.direction: dollar up with yields up = growth

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the term premium across the board is starting to move from negative to positive
claims.claim: Term premia are turning positive across the curve, a trend that points to higher yields because deficits, QT and global financing needs demand compensation.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: China That's while they have new fiscal policy that they're fa facing what we call a balance sheet recession
claims.claim: China's balance sheet recession means firms use cash to pay down debt, so its fiscal stimulus does not boost spending as much.

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: swap spreads have been trading lower relative to bond yields of late
claims.claim: Swap spreads falling reflect expectations that Treasuries get lighter bank capital treatment (supplementary leverage ratio relief) to support demand for bonds.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: do we have a shortage of safe assets
claims.claim: A shortage of Treasuries as collateral, plus FX risk for foreign buyers and higher rate volatility (MOVE above VIX), makes Treasuries riskier than before.

correction.issue: Merges two points and implies the safe-asset shortage makes Treasuries riskier; Mark says regulation/collateral demand makes Treasuries a (possibly scarce) safe asset, while FX risk and higher rate volatility are what make holding them riskier.
correction.fix: Treasuries are a safe asset partly because regulation creates collateral demand (raising the question of a safe-asset shortage), but FX risk for foreign buyers and higher rate volatility (MOVE more volatile than VIX) make holding them riskier than before.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: I've done some analysis on this i s of say that uh Trend following models do work in
claims.claim: Trend following models work in cryptocurrencies.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: what is the risk cycle which is different than the business cycle
claims.claim: The risk cycle (volatility, leverage, risk appetite) is distinct from the business cycle and should be monitored separately; volatility has been low apart from August 2024.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you don't get the cross margining that you would like
claims.claim: Allocators are cautious on crypto-only trend programs because of operational issues (prime broker, no cross margining) and thin liquidity that caps capacity and raises costs beyond the top coins.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: is is that low uh volatility actually be gets uh more leverage
claims.claim: The risk cycle differs from the business cycle: persistent low volatility, especially low downside volatility, invites leverage and risk-taking that plant the seeds of a later shock.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you have to look at what happened prior to the spike in the vix rise
claims.claim: Harm from a volatility spike depends on prior low volatility and the leverage of players like hedge funds and CTAs, so watch how volatility propagates through leverage.
claims.indicator: VIX; leverage of hedge funds and CTAs

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: credit spreads are extreme extremely tight
claims.claim: Credit spreads are extremely tight even as card and auto delinquencies rise and small-cap earnings are poor, suggesting equilibrium spreads should be higher.

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: we had obviously you know a blip in 2022
claims.claim: Credit spread spikes in 2022 and 2020 may have blunted leverage buildup compared with the uninterrupted late-1990s low spreads.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: a lot of them all refinance to fixed rate mortgages in the US at at low rates
claims.claim: US consumers hold fixed low-rate mortgages (housing gridlock), while floating-rate countries outside the US are more exposed to higher rates.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you are going to have spikes that's not the issue the issue is is that when you have low periods of low volatility
claims.claim: Leverage uses assets as collateral, so a shock lowers collateral value; embedded leverage raises sensitivity to the shock.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: prices are Primal so prices are the most important thing to look at first
claims.claim: A trend follower should look first at prices while treating other information as supplementary.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you can resolve information uncertainty I give you the headlines but you can't resolve or uh reaction or behavioral uncertainty
claims.claim: Even perfect next-day headlines gave marginal returns in the Elm Capitalist experiment: knowing news does not tell you the market reaction, so a trend follower focuses on price.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: a kind environment would be is is that there's a good link between you know the action and then the response
claims.claim: Kind learning environments have clear cause-effect feedback; markets are wicked (inconsistent relationships), so experience can mislead (Hogarth).
claims.conditions: wicked: relation between inflation and bonds not one-for-one

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: Trend following is more observational as opposed to causal in how they build the models
claims.claim: Trend following avoids hard causal inference in macro and relies on observed price persistence; machine-learning approaches suffer when learned relationships break down.
claims.conditions: when relationships are unstable ML fails more

correction.issue: Wrong speaker for part of the claim: the point that machine-learning strategies suffer when learned relationships break down was made by the host Alan Dunne, not Mark.
correction.fix: Mark: trend following is observational, not causal; it avoids hard causal inference in macro and relies on observed price persistence. (Alan: machine-learning strategies learned from past relationships suffer when those relationships break down.)

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: the Cal relationships themselves are are are not not necessarily consistent
claims.claim: Causal macro relations flip over time (bad news is good news, then good news is good news).

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you can be an average forecaster but if you're very good at position sizing and risk management you can survive and still make money
claims.claim: Good position sizing and risk management matter as much as forecast skill: average forecasters survive with sizing, great forecasters with poor sizing still go bankrupt (55/45 accuracy is good).

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: most of these models are actually EX look at trailing PE though
claims.claim: FINRA-required analyst model disclosures show most analysts value stocks with trailing P/E multiples then tweak it, not discounted forward earnings.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we find we have post earnings drift and we as have Trend following some stocks
claims.claim: Backward-looking analysts adjust valuations slowly as new earnings arrive, explaining post-earnings drift and stock trends.
claims.direction: stocks drift in direction of surprise

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there's actually an underreaction in stocks
claims.claim: LLM-aggregated news narrative trends (State Street product) predict stock returns because of underreaction and slow information diffusion; trends in news lead trends in prices.
claims.direction: trade in the direction of news sentiment trend

claims.speaker: Alan
claims.quote: investors do underreact to uh news early on in the trend and later on over overreact
claims.claim: Anchoring means investors underreact to news early in a trend and overreact later, one base of trend-following profit.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: as long as the price action is behaving the same it says yes I'm going to continue to follow that
claims.claim: Post-election themes (tax cuts, deregulation, deficits) combined with trending fundamentals suggest trends continue as long as price action confirms; stop out otherwise.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: I've always sort of think of this as more Dynamic uh beta
claims.claim: Trend following is dynamic beta (positive, negative or zero) rather than crisis alpha or unpredictable alpha.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you should probably increase your allocation a trend following a high interest rate environment
claims.claim: Quantica research: increase allocation to trend following in high-rate regimes: more dispersion and volatility, and lower correlation to bonds and equities.
claims.indicator: trend following vs interest rate level
claims.direction: overweight trend following when rates are high

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the correlation between ctas and bonds gets lower and the correlation is slightly slower for equities
claims.claim: In high-rate regimes CTA correlation to bonds and equities falls, making trend following a better diversifier than clipping bond coupons.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: certain techniques um that you can be able to bundle a set of strategies and come up with a replication strategy
claims.claim: Corey Hoffstein-type replication can mimic the BTOP 50 by bundling strategies, but dispersion among trend followers makes replicating skill hard; interest from swap providers and allocators.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you almost have to look at an ensemble of of tables for that valuation discussion and when you look at the Ensemble you're going to get a mixed reports but generally all of them are moving in the same direction
claims.claim: A single equity-risk-premium chart should not be trusted alone; judge valuation from an ensemble of measures, which disagree in level but here all point the same way (ERP declining).
claims.indicator: ensemble of equity risk premium / valuation measures
claims.testable: yes - build several ERP measures and test a composite vs single measures

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: so I would say a bit of a choppier picture on the Comm on the commodi side but certainly currencies and financials trending
claims.claim: In November 2024 currencies and financial futures trended (helping trend followers) while commodities were choppy (gold reversing sharply, grains choppy), and bonds had been choppy for trend followers earlier in 2024.
claims.direction: trend profits from currencies and financials, not commodities
claims.testable: yes - sector attribution of trend returns

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: some of that is is because of construction
claims.claim: Part of the VIX decline before the election was mechanical, a result of how the VIX is constructed (its fixed forward window), not only a fall in uncertainty.
claims.conditions: around scheduled events entering or leaving the VIX window
claims.testable: partly - compare VIX with event-adjusted implied vol term structure

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it feels like every time bond yields go up people start hoping with de and deficits again and then when they go down they kind of forget about it
claims.claim: The debt-and-deficit narrative follows bond yields: it gains attention when yields rise and is forgotten when they fall; 10-year yields have ranged roughly 4% to 5% and sit near 4.6%, toward the top.
claims.testable: partly - news-attention counts vs yield changes

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: we had some comments from po last night I think kind of uh stampen expectations or further red Cuts in in December
claims.claim: Powell's comments dampened expectations of further Fed cuts in December 2024 because the economy is strong.
claims.testable: yes - fed funds futures around speech

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: it has some usefulness is also sort of uh mixed uh because it it really does you know bounce around a lot
claims.claim: In Mark's own research the Bloom news-based policy uncertainty indices have some usefulness but are a mixed, noisy signal because they bounce around a lot.
claims.testable: yes - smoothing and predictive tests of EPU

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: markets are trading on what we're seeing in the high frequency data
claims.claim: After the election, markets trade on strong high-frequency data and on broad expected policies (tax cuts, deregulation, tariffs, deportations) whose details are not yet known, which drives small-cap moves.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: when rates were very low and then there is this negative correlation between stocks and bonds term premium was was negative or there was no term premium
claims.claim: Long yields decompose into real yield (long-term growth), expected inflation and a term premium; in the low-rate regime with negative stock-bond correlation the term premium was zero or negative, and it rises when bonds stop hedging.
claims.direction: term premium up when stock-bond correlation turns positive
claims.conditions: low rates and negative stock-bond correlation -> negative term premium
claims.testable: yes - ACM term premium vs rolling stock-bond correlation

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we know that generally is is that the higher the level of rates the higher the volatility of rates
claims.claim: Rate volatility rises with the level of rates, so a move to a higher yield band raises the risk of holding Treasuries.
claims.indicator: yield level vs MOVE index / realized rate volatility
claims.testable: yes - regress rate vol on yield level

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if you held them in the uh Your Mark to mark market account as opposed to your book value account all of a sudden you find out as said wow this is blowing a hole in my balance sheet
claims.claim: Silicon Valley Bank shows the real duration risk of Treasuries: banks that put deposit inflows into long Treasuries took large mark-to-market losses when rates rose, so more capital should be held against them.
claims.conditions: rapid rate rises after deposit-funded duration buying

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the traditional view of a trend follower is this is it well I really don't care what the asset is as long as it Trends
claims.claim: Classic trend following is market-agnostic and diversified (any trending, tradable symbol, often 50+ markets), so a crypto-only trend program departs from the usual many-market principle.
claims.testable: yes - breadth vs Sharpe of trend portfolios

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the move has been higher and then I think that that has a lot to do with the inflation and and uh pivoting by the FED
claims.claim: Bond volatility (MOVE) has stayed high relative to equity volatility (VIX) because of inflation and uncertainty over Fed pivots.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: so now that you're going to have to S you got to clean up your balance sheet and then that really has an impact in what on your future growth
claims.claim: After years of strong growth and leverage build-up, a shock forces balance-sheet repair that lowers future growth (China now, like Japan in the early 1990s; caption says China).
claims.conditions: after a leverage boom followed by a shock

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there are themes or memes that start to occur that could cause uh excesses in valuation that lead to Bubbles and then crashes
claims.claim: Following Shiller, popular themes or memes can drive valuation excesses that become bubbles and then crashes.
claims.testable: partly - narrative indices vs valuation and crash risk

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the barriers to entry are really high you got to spend a lot of work to be able to do this there's a lot of data you have to process it
claims.claim: News-narrative signals are costly to build (large data and processing effort), so for most managers they are at best an adjunct to price trends rather than a core signal.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: results came out boom you had this big jump in price but then as you know even even in that when you look at the narrative we're starting to develop themes
claims.claim: News underreaction is an average effect: a big event such as the election can be priced in an immediate jump, after which themes develop gradually and can still feed trends (answering Alan's doubt that the move was an underreaction).
claims.indicator: event-day returns vs later narrative trend
claims.conditions: large scheduled events produce jumps first
claims.testable: yes - post-event drift after large jumps

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if you're a large allocator you may say that well I just want to get the average because I don't want to pick the bad manager
claims.claim: Large allocators may prefer trend replication or trend beta to get the average CTA return and avoid manager-selection risk, accepting that skill is not replicated.
